articles.title: Croatia 0-7 England: Amazing Nations League win as Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each score twice in huge victory
articles.summary: Match report as England put SEVEN past Croatia in Rijeka in an emphatic victory in their Nations League Group A3 fixture; Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice while Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers were also on target for the Three Lions
articles.body:
In what must surely rank as one of England's best away results, Thomas Tuchel's side utterly overwhelmed their opponents. Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored two each but it was a stunning team performance that inflicted Croatia's biggest defeat.

The skipper opened the scoring by firing high into the roof of the net early on after being well fed by Jude Bellingham before Anthony Gordon's ingenuity engineered the second for Bellingham to score himself soon after. England were rampant from the outset.

The excellent Gordon had chances of his own before making it three. There had been some disquiet that Jarell Quansah had been preferred to Trent Alexander-Arnold but the Bayer Leverkusen man whipped in a quality cross for the Barcelona winger to nod in a third.

When Bellingham set up Bukayo Saka for the fourth before the break, Slaven Bilic looked shocked. Although Mateo Kovacic did miss a sitter, the score did not flatter England. It was an 'I-was-there moment' for the 100 away fans allowed in the stadium.

Croatia tried to be more aggressive after the break but a sensational team goal underlined England's superiority as Kane latched onto Elliot Anderson's cross to make it five. Saka soon latched onto an error for the sixth and Morgan Rogers capped it off late on.

Tuchel needed a strong showing during this quartet of Nations League games that concludes with a home game against the Czech Republic on Tuesday. The opening defeat to Spain followed by a win over a Czech side reduced to 10 men was insufficient.

This was as convincing as it gets against a Croatia team, led by Luka Modric, that looked unable to compete with the speed, strength and skill of an England side that included Alex Scott from the start for the first time. This was a significant win in Group A3 too.

With World Cup winners Spain currently boasting the perfect record, there is likely to be only more space available to qualify for the last eight of the Nations League in the spring. This win goes some way to securing that spot for England. A big boost for Tuchel.

8 - GOAL! Kane fired home after being fed by Bellingham

21 - GOAL! Bellingham made it two from Gordon's assist

39 - GOAL! Gordon headed in Quansah's right-wing cross

41 - HOWLER! Kovacic missed an open goal for Croatia

45 - GOAL! Bellingham set up Saka for England's fourth

53 - GOAL! Kane latched onto Anderson's cross to score

68 - GOAL! Stanisic's error gifted Saka England's sixth goal

87 - GOAL! Rogers raced through to cap off incredible win

England head coach Thomas Tuchel speaking to ITV Sport:

"Maybe there were three minutes after 3-0 where we had a big mistake and some easy ball losses but that was a 90-minute performance on a high level from everyone, from the first minute to the last minute, from everyone who started to everyone who came off the bench. It was the highest level and congratulations to the team.

"On an away pitch, very, very impressive. We created so many chances. We were so fluid from the start. I remember looking at the clock and thinking, wow, this has been a good first three minutes and then I looked again and it was a good first seven minutes and it just never stopped.

"We just kept the pace up, played through the gaps and were very, very clinical. We stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending so we did the basics right. I loved the attitude. We always played humble. We always got the basics right and that is why it was a complete performance."

"Everything you would want. A complete performance in possession. Goal threat. Scored the seven goals. Kept a clean sheet. Hunting in packs when they lost the ball.

"England were clinical as well. Excellent. All the plaudits have to go to England. They were fantastic.

"Bellingham can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time. There's still a lot more to come from him. He's a huge leader for England."

On the day that the England captain moved within one cap of Peter Shilton's record, Kane scored for the third consecutive game in this Nations League break. With six goals in his last five games for Bayern Munich too, his relentlessness really is remarkable.

Fresh from scoring 73 goals all competitions for club and country last season, Kane has now netted in each of his last six away appearances for his country, with only three men previously having scored in that many consecutive away matches for the Three Lions.

The most recent of those was Stan Mortensen in 1948 and the only man to score in seven matches in a row is Tom Finney. Kane will need to score away from home against Spain next month to match that particular feat. On this form, do not rule that out.

'No better team in world football to watch'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett at the Stadion HNK Rijeka:

"England sank Croatia without a trace on the Adriatic coast, with the Good Ship Tuchel now full steam ahead after the World Cup supporter mutiny.

"No one could have predicted a performance of this utter dominance against the team ranked 14 in the world.

"England cut through a woeful Croatia midfield and defence at will, like a red hot knife carves through softened butter, and Tuchel's front men had a field day.

"Two goals for Captain Kane with an assist to boot. Two goals for Saka, which will have been a timely confidence-boost for the Arsenal man. There was a goal and a hat-trick of assists for the irrepressible Jude Bellingham, alongside a goal and an assist for the equally magnificent Anthony Gordon.

"Croatia were simply blown away, and England could have won by more.

"When England are rampaging all over the pitch like this, wining back possession when they have no right to do so, passing forward at every opportunity and finishing ruthlessly, there is no better team in world football to watch.

"Seven-nil in Rijeka does not flatter them. This was a statement victory, and a marker of what they are capable of."

England's upcoming Nations League Group A3 fixtures

Tuesday October 6 : Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm

Thursday November 12 : Croatia (H), kick-off 7.45pm

Sunday November 15 : Spain (A), kick-off 7.45pm

articles.title: Belichick, UNC vs. Freeman, Carr, Notre Dame Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: The No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish further cemented their status as national championship contenders on Saturday, beating the North Carolina Tar Heels 37-26 at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.
articles.body:
The No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish further cemented their status as national championship contenders on Saturday, beating the North Carolina Tar Heels 37-26 at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

Notre Dame entered the game as a 19.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and after falling behind 7-0 early in the first quarter, the Fighting Irish established dominance by reeling off 21 unanswered points, although North Carolina tightened things up late in the first half and early in the second.

UNC had no answers for Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr and wide receiver Jordan Faison, who torched head coach Bill Belichick's defense. Here is a rundown of the key statistical performers from Saturday's game:

After the Irish punted on their opening drive, North Carolina marched quickly down the field, culminating in a six-yard touchdown pass from Billy Edwards Jr. to Shamar Easter:

Notre Dame began to pour it on from there, though, as Carr threw a pair of spectacular touchdown passes to Faison with a 12-yard scoring toss to Jaden Greathouse sandwiched in between over ND's next three offensive drives:

The Tar Heels seized some momentum back before halftime with a 14-yard touchdown pass from Edwards to tight end Jelani Thurman with 21 seconds left in the second quarter:

That momentum carried over into the second half, as Jaden Jefferson started the third quarter off with a bang, returning the kickoff 98 yards for a touchdown:

The Tar Heels fumbled the snap on the extra point, allowing Notre Dame to maintain a one-point lead.

Notre Dame had an emphatic answer, tailoring a 17-play, 75-yard drive that took over nine minutes off the clock. The Irish converted three fourth downs on the drive, including a three-yard touchdown run by Carr on fourth-and-goal:

However, like North Carolina, Notre Dame botched the extra-point attempt with an errant snap, so the ND lead sat at seven.

The Fighting Irish put the game out of reach on their next two drives, as Carr accounted for his fifth total touchdown of the day on a six-yard pass to Nolan James Jr. before Notre Dame added a field goal to make it 37-20.

UNC made the score look a bit better cosmetically when Thurman found the end zone for a second time, but with 2:36 remaining in the game, there wasn't enough time to make a comeback.

It wasn't always easy for the Irish on Saturday, but they improved to 5-0 on the season with an impressive victory.

Head coach Marcus Freeman's team looked unstoppable at times on offense, which is why they are a popular pick to run the table in the College Football Playoff.

As for the Tar Heels, they are now 2-2 following a 2-0 start, and some of the optimism that existed early in the season is starting to wane.

UNC will try to bounce back next week when it goes on the road to face Pittsburgh, while Notre Dame will host Stanford next Saturday.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham: England and Real Madrid star tipped for greatness after Croatia thrashing by Roy Keane
articles.summary: England inflicted Croatia's biggest defeat in a 7-0 hammering in the Nations League with Jude Bellingham scoring one goal and setting up three more in a complete performance from the Real Madrid star who continues to shine for the Three Lions after his World Cup heroics
articles.body:
The 23-year-old scored one goal and set up three more as England inflicted Croatia's biggest defeat in a 7-0 hammering in front of a reduced crowd in Rijeka in the Nations League.

Bellingham was England's standout player at the World Cup and has become the focal point of Thomas Tuchel's side, registering 13 goal involvements in his last 11 games since the start of the tournament.

Keane heaped praise on Bellingham after the win over Croatia and said it was a complete performance from a player who has become a "huge leader for England".

"There's still a lot more to come from [Bellingham]," Keane said on ITV .

"Bellingham can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time.

"His attitude for England recently...I have been praising him for being fantastic in possession, but what he is doing out of possession, that lifts all these players.

"If you have a player who is that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and is playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball, that will inspire all the other players."

Keane said England made Croatia, who are ranked 14th in the world, look like a "Gibraltar-type of team".

On England's performance, Keane added: "Everything you would want. A complete performance."

Saka: 'Special' Bellingham deserved man of the match

Bukayo Saka, who scored two goals for Tuchel's side in Croatia, was in full agreement with Keane as he hailed the impact of England's men's player of the year for 2025/26.

"It was an amazing night for us," Saka told ITV . "We played with high energy and spirit and punished them tonight.

"He [Bellingham] was amazing tonight to be fair. He deserved player of the year and he probably deserves man of the match tonight as well. He was special. Happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."

Tuchel concurred with one reporter after the game that Bellingham had gone to to the "next level" but warned that "you can never stand still" in football.

Asked if he felt Bellingham had taken a step up in his performances, Tuchel said: "Yes, at the moment it seems like [that] and you always need to.

"The level that you showed last week is never enough in the next week, that's just the nature of football. We adjusted some things, gave the players a lot of responsibility and they are a group to be trusted.

"It was impressive. It was the first time that this group played like this together again and they were very good and the translation from the last two matches, from the training sessions and the meetings into this match was on the highest level."

Kane & Tuchel on England's formidable front four

Tuchel has landed on a formidable front four of Harry Kane and Bellingham flanked either side by Saka and Anthony Gordon.

All four were on the scoresheet against Croatia, who were completely overwhelmed by England's firepower.

Of the front four, captain Kane told ITV : "There's freedom. All four of us are good players, we can play in the 10 pocket, Ant can play as a No 9, B can come in as a No 10, Jude can play as a No 9, I can play as a midfielder.

"It's so hard for the opposition to pick it up. The bottom line is if you lose the ball, we're all smart enough and good enough to cover in midfield or defence.

"That's the way we want to play. For them it was so hard to pick a man and press."

Explaining why the front four were so impressive, England boss Tuchel added: "The support from the full-backs, of course, and then the movements through the last line were on the highest level today.

"They get better and better. That's why I didn't want to change so much from match to match, to get the fluidity going and to get the movements going and to get the automatisms right within the front four but they are very good together at the moment.

"They enjoy playing together and the work rate is on a high level and the counter-press is on a high level so these are complete performances.

"The full-backs keep on pushing and supporting and the midfielders keep on pushing and supporting, so it's always a team effort, but the front four look very dangerous at the moment."

Analysis: Is there a better nation in world football to watch?

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett at Stadion HNK Rijeka:

"England sank Croatia without a trace on the Adriatic coast, with the Good Ship Tuchel now full steam ahead after the World Cup supporter mutiny.

"No one could have predicted a performance of this utter dominance against the team ranked 14 in the world.

"England cut through a woeful Croatia midfield and defence at will, like a red hot knife carves through softened butter, and Tuchel's front men had a field day.

"Two goals for Captain Kane with an assist to boot. Two goals for Saka, which will have been a timely confidence boost for the Arsenal man. There was a goal and a hat-trick of assists for the irrepressible Jude Bellingham, alongside a goal and an assist for the equally magnificent Anthony Gordon.

"Croatia were simply blown away, and England could have won by more.

"When England are rampaging all over the pitch like this, wining back possession when they have no right to do so, passing forward at every opportunity and finishing ruthlessly, there is no better team in world football to watch.

"Seven-nil in Rijeka does not flatter them. This was a statement victory, and a marker of what they are capable of."

articles.title: Bryce Underwood, Michigan Upset by Minnesota, Kyle Whittingham's Updated Contract Buyout
articles.summary: Things are not going well for Bryce Underwood and Kyle Whittingham right now, as Michigan fell 20-14 to Minnesota on Saturday for its second consecutive loss.
articles.body:
Things are not going well for Bryce Underwood and Kyle Whittingham right now, as Michigan fell 20-14 to Minnesota on Saturday for its second consecutive loss.

Underwood, the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2025 recruiting class, finished 10-of-21 for 101 yards passing with two interceptions and no touchdowns against Minnesota.

Whittingham, who left Utah after 22 seasons to become Michigan's head coach, signed a five-year, $41 million contract in December.

Per Tony Garcia of the Detroit Free Press , specific details of Whittingham's deal stipulate he would be owed 75 percent of the money remaining on his contract if he were to be fired without cause.

While the Wolverines have played largely uninspired football so far this season, Minnesota head coach P.J. Fleck was more than happy to revel in the glow of his team's first home win over its Big Ten rival since 1977.

Whittingham's tenure at Utah was often up and down, but the highs were incredibly high. It included a 13-0 record in 2008 and eight seasons of at least 10 wins.

The Utes had a total of three 10-win seasons from 1905 to 2004.

If one were to mount a defense for Whittingham right now, he did take over a program that is still loaded with players who were recruited by Sherrone Moore's staff.

The transfer portal didn't produce huge results for Whittingham with a total of 17 incoming players this season.

Michigan's biggest problem is Underwood has not come close to living up to the hype that followed him as a high school prospect. He threw for 2,423 yards, 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions as a true freshman last year.

This season has been a step back in some ways for Underwood. He set season-lows in completion percentage (47.6), passing yards (101) and yards per attempt (4.8) on Saturday.

Michigan's offense has been held under 20 points in four of the first five games. Its lone game over that mark was against a UTEP defense that entered today with the fifth-worst defense in FBS by points allowed per game.

True freshman Tommy Carr is the Wolverines' backup quarterback. He was a 4-star recruit and No. 22 quarterback prospect in the 2026 class, per 247Sports' composite rankings .

Carr might not be a significant upgrade over Underwood at this point given his lack of experience, but the offense has been such a mess through five games that it can't hurt to see if things might improve with someone else under center.

Michigan is off next week before hosting Penn State and Indiana in back-to-back weeks.

articles.title: Rodri canta gol más de dos años después
articles.standfirst: Firma el 2-0 y su quinta diana con la selección
articles.summary: Firma el 2-0 y su quinta diana con la selección
articles.body: Rodri levantó la Copa del Mundo en el MetLife. El gran momento de su vida. El Mundial era su obsesión. Su cara de felicidad al ofrecer el trofeo en Sevilla y en Oviedo lo explica todo. Dos fiestas en las que el capitán de España ha dejado su huella con un gol. A los 35 minutos del duelo ante la República Checa, cuando el equipo de Santi Denia había lanzado algún mensaje de poder pelear el partido, Rodri apareció en el área para aprovechar un balón muerto y hacer imposible el intento desesperado de Kinsky de escapar del 2-0. La relación de Rodri con el gol no es intensa, aunque uno suyo le dio al Manchester City la única Champions que tiene. Su cuenta de goles con España se limita a cinco. El primero fue en el 6-0 a Alemania en noviembre de 2020, aún con Luis Enrique como seleccionador. Los otros cuatro son desde la llegada de Luis de la Fuente, el entrenador que le entregó el mando absoluto del juego de España. En marzo de 2024, ante Brasil, marcó dos veces de penalti en un partido que acabó 3-3. Se jugó horas después de la muerte de su abuelo. Morata le cedió el brazalete de capitán. Y también fueron para él los dos penaltis que tuvo la selección española. En la Euro ganada el 14 de julio en Berlín aparece un gol de Rodri. No fue uno más. Porque sacó a España del atolladero en el que se había metido en los octavos de final, ante Georgia. Un disparo suyo fue el 1-1 y rescató a la selección de un ataque de pánico. Ese gol y su orden de que se calmaran todos llevó el partido al lugar que se esperaba y al 4-1 final. Eso fue el 30 de junio de 2024. Luego llegó la grave lesión. Meses de oscuridad, el regreso a la selección en septiembre de 2025, otra zona oscura y, al fin, el Rodri de verdad en un crecimiento que le llevó a ser elegido el mejor jugador del Mundial. El gol ante los checos tenía el valor de asegurar la victoria, las rachas de España y la puerta a que De la Fuente moviera el equipo de cara al partido de Split.

articles.title: Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor's Box Score Stats, Highlights, Heisman Hype from Alabama vs. MSU
articles.summary: The battle of early-season Heisman contenders went decidedly in Keelon Russell's favor as Alabama, which entered favored by 5.5 points on FanDuel Sportsbook, ran all over Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State in a 56-23 win at Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday.
articles.body:
The battle of early-season Heisman contenders went decidedly in Keelon Russell's favor as Alabama, which entered favored by 5.5 points on FanDuel Sportsbook , ran all over Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State in a 56-23 win at Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday.

Russell accounted for four touchdowns with no turnovers before being pulled midway through the fourth quarter with the game in hand.

Taylor did rebound somewhat after a disastrous start that included a lost fumble and interception on his first two offensive possessions, but he left the game late with an injury.

The Crimson Tide scored 14 points in every quarter. They got touchdowns on their first two offensive possessions plus a pick-six in between to take a commanding 21-7 lead seven seconds into the second quarter.

Russell had no shortage of highlight moments in the game, but the best sequence came on the second touchdown drive. He had a 39-yard pass to Lotzeir Brooks on third-and-19 that set up his 17-yard touchdown run three plays later.

After a slow start to the season with one touchdown pass and two interceptions through the first two games, Russell has caught fire over the last three weeks to put Alabama on the short list of best teams in the nation.

This game could not have started worse for Taylor and Mississippi State. He was strip-sacked on the fifth play of the game, then followed up with a pick-six on the third play of the Bulldogs' next drive.

Taylor was seen walking toward the locker room midway through the fourth quarter with an apparent injury.

Taylor did help get Mississippi State back within one score at 21-14 midway through the second quarter. Alabama would score touchdowns on three consecutive possessions at the end of the first half and start of the second half to put the game away.

After entering the day with 14 touchdowns and two interceptions, Taylor matched his interception total through the first four weeks in this game alone. He also had his lowest completion percentage (55.9) and fewest yards per attempt (7.6) all season.

Taylor will have an opportunity to recover with the Bulldogs off next week before returning to play on Oct. 17 at LSU.

Alabama is back in action next week in one of the marquee games of the season against No. 2 Georgia at Bryant-Denny Stadium.

articles.title: Cárdenas: "Los futbolistas estamos en un punto intermedio que poco podemos hacer"
articles.standfirst: El portero compareció en el evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab horas después de disputar el amistoso jugado en Vallecas
articles.summary: El portero compareció en el evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab tras el amistoso jugado en Vallecas
articles.body: Dani Cárdenas fue uno de los protagonistas del evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab organizado en Los Ángeles de San Rafael desde donde comentó en primera persona todo lo sucedido en el amistoso jugador en Vallecas horas antes. Pregunta: ¿Cómo se vivió la situación previa al partido desde dentro? Respuesta: Al final, creo que los futbolistas nos hemos centrado en poder competir en este partido. Para algunos, como yo en este caso, son minutos que tenemos que hacer válidos, que tenemos que aprovechar. Evidentemente, nos gustaría que la situación fuese otra, que la gente pudiese ir de verdad al estadio a disfrutar del fútbol, a poder animar al equipo, como innumerables veces hacen. Pero sí que es cierto que, al final, el ruido llega, nos enteramos de todo. Y yo creo que, al final, poco podemos hacer nosotros. Estamos en un punto intermedio en el cual el futbolista, yo creo que tenemos que dar lo máximo para que la afición esté contenta con nosotros y, sobre todo, respetar el escudo que llevamos. P: ¿Hubo alguna amenaza por parte de Bukaneros de boicotear el partido? R: Yo creo que no ha habido ningún movimiento de Bukaneros o, por lo menos, no me ha llegado a mí nada de ruido esto. Por desgracia, yo creo que desde que llevo aquí, la lucha que tienen ha continuado, no es algo nuevo para nosotros. P: ¿Cómo afecta a nivel deportivo esta situación a la plantilla? R: Si algo tengo claro es que Vallecas es su gente, el Rayo es su gente. Vienen a disfrutar, vienen a animar, como no he podido vivir en otro estadio de local. Y nada, esperemos que sea el primer partido de este año en Vallecas. P: ¿Qué esperas de Vallecas tras el parón? R: Que tengamos un año desde hoy hasta el final de temporada jugando de local en Vallecas, disfrutando de nuestra gente y que nuestra gente se sienta orgullosa y disfrutando de nosotros.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Keelon Russell Rises, Kamario Taylor Falls
articles.summary: Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell became the betting favorite to win the 2026 Heisman Trophy following an impressive performance in the No. 7 Crimson Tide's 56-23 road win over the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs on Saturday.
articles.body:
Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell became the betting favorite to win the 2026 Heisman Trophy following an impressive performance in the No. 7 Crimson Tide's 56-23 road win over the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs on Saturday.

Russell nudged past Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith to become the new favorite. Here is where things currently stand regarding the Heisman odds, courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook :

Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State: +3000

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State: +3500

Expert CFB Locks for Week 5's Biggest Games 🔒

Russell turned in another dominant performance on Saturday, going 16-of-22 for 285 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions, while also rushing for 16 yards and a touchdown.

The sophomore signal-caller has Bama off to a 5-0 start, and he has been especially strong over the past three games, which saw the Tide beat Florida State, South Carolina and Mississippi State.

Per Bryan Fischer of Sports Illustrated , Russell has been nearly perfect during that stretch, accounting for 13 total touchdowns and no interceptions:

While Russell strengthened his Heisman case Saturday, Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor saw his take a hit.

Taylor entered Saturday's contest having thrown 14 touchdown passes and just two interceptions on the season. In the loss to Alabama, he managed to throw for 258 yards and another three scores, but he was picked off twice, including a pick-six.

There is a clear separation in the Heisman race with four players at 7-1 odds or better and six at 13-1 or better. After Florida running back Jadan Baugh at 13-1, the next closest players sit at 30-1.

Russell may indeed be the player to beat for the Heisman right now, but he has some tough competition.

Smith entered play Saturday with a remarkable 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns through just four games, while Darian Mensah and CJ Carr have led their teams to undefeated starts and look like national title contenders.

articles.title: Con la facilidad de Messi
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del España - República Checa
articles.summary: La contracrónica del España - República Checa
articles.body: Lamine recibió, levantó la cabeza y puso el balón directamente en la escuadra para hacer el 1-0. Sin carrerilla, sin aparente esfuerzo, sin darle importancia. En el minuto 6. El crack de la selección cada día se parece más a Messi a la hora de hacer que lo extraordinario parezca sencillo. Juega como el chaval que se sienta a jugar con la Play y sabe que puede hacer lo que quiera con los botones. Regatea, acelera, frena y coloca la pelota donde quiere. España, y esta es una de las principales diferencias con los campeones de 2010, tiene un futbolista único. No fue el mejor partido de España, pero aún así dejó minutos, sobre todo en la primera parte, de un nivel inalcanzable para el resto. Cuando la selección coge el hilo y empieza a tocar al primer toque a toda velocidad, no hay quien frene a este equipo. España ganó 3-1 y hasta sufrió un poco, pero analizando la totalidad del encuentro pudo imponerse por muchos goles más. Hasta cuando no firma un partido redondo, el nivel que alcanza es sobresaliente. En la España de Luis de la Fuente, Baena se ha convertido en un pilar. Da gusto verle. Con la selección saca todos sus trucos y regala todo tipo de controles y asistencias al primer toque que ponen en pie al estadio y que le pillan todos sus socios de alrededor. Baena, Rodri, Olmo, Lamine, Pedri, Fabián... lo del centro del campo de España es de locos. La mano española se empieza a notar en la República Checa. Santi Denia y Pablo Amo han empezado a dejar su sello en una selección que, pese a sufrir durante muchos minutos el vendaval de España, aguantó de pie y trató de no renunciar nunca al balón. No era precisamente un escenario para lucirse, pero dejó algunas pinceladas interesantes y con el 2-1, un golazo, metió la incertidumbre al equipo de De la Fuente. En esta República Checa siempre hay intención de jugar, de salir con el balón y de construir desde atrás incluso cuando enfrente está una España que con su presión apenas concede tiempo para respirar. Fresneda y Fran García, dos laterales que no estaban en la lista inicial, fueron titulares ante la República Checa. Y los dos se marcaron un partidazo. Fran, en su línea habitual, fue un avión, mostrándose superior físicamente en cada duelo y en cada arrancada. Fresneda jugó como si llevara un buen puñado de internacionalidades a sus espaldas, como si llevara toda la vida jugando por detrás de Lamine Yamal. Otros dos ejemplos de que este equipo funciona juegue quien juegue. España, que encajó un gol en todo el Mundial,. ya ha recibido cuatro en los tres primeros partidos de la Liga de las Naciones. No es un drama. Y de hecho, posiblemente, sea lo normal. Lo que no fue normal fue la racha de España en el Mundial y la concentración defensiva que tuvo todo el equipo durante la Copa del Mundo. Un ejercicio defensivo perfecto que probablemente no se volverá a ver en un Mundial. Y no son cinco los goles encajados porque el colegiado del encuentro vio una faltita de Sadilek sobre Le Normand con la que anuló el gol del empate checo, que llegó tras un error garrafal de Raya. Al portero de España se le escapó el balón sobre la línea de gol y se lo dejó a Naderi para que remachara el balón a la red. El colegiado vio un agarrón en la frontal del área y anuló el gol de la República Checa para incredulidad de Santi Denia.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal se deja de gaitas
articles.standfirst: El zurdo abre pronto con un golazo una sufrida victoria de España, que se dejó ir antes de tiempo ante la República Checa
articles.summary: El zurdo abre pronto con un golazo una sufrida victoria de España, que se dejó ir antes de tiempo ante la República Checa
articles.body: Llevaba España cinco minutos sin hacer un gol, una minicrisis en este paraíso, cuando Lamine Yamal se perfiló y regaló a los fotógrafos un escuadrazo. Fue lo mejor de un partido en el que España sacó la almohada antes de tiempo. Es el problema de sentirse más guapo y poderoso que el de enfrente. El partido iba para pasatiempo tras el chicharro de Lamine, acompañado de otra diana de Rodri, pero los checos, cuando se quitaron las cadenas, rozaron el Panenkazo en el Tartiere. Hicieron un gol y se les anuló otro tras pifia de Raya, aunque el árbitro había pitado antes. Los checos se sintieron estafados y terminaron el encuentro con un mosqueo que llegaba a Praga. Krejci se ganó la expulsión y el final fue poco decoroso. Merino, como figura en los guiones, se casó otra vez con la red para sentenciar el choque. De la Fuente auguró un tantarantán cercano para España. El problema es que en el ambiente se ha instalado la sensación de que es fácil sacar todos los días matrícula de honor. En la segunda parte, con los cambios y la relajación, el equipo se dejó el equilibrio y el orden en la caseta. El inicio fue otra película. Poco tardó España en quitar el balón, el partido y las espinilleras a los checos. Es la especialidad de la casa. En el mediocampo se juntaban Rodri, Pedri, Olmo y Baena, que es como llevar la pelota a una sala secreta del Pentágono. Para quitarle el mando a la selección española se necesita una banda organizada de forajidos. Los checos han puesto el proyecto en manos de Santi Denia, campeón olímpico en París, poca broma y supuesto antídoto para De la Fuente, con el que compartió muchas horas en las tuberías de Las Rozas. Uno y otro disponen de distinto material. Santi habría pagado por cambiar cinco minutos el banquillo. El seleccionador español sólo mantuvo a Lamine y Baena de los que golearon a Croacia. En los laterales, nuevos propietarios. En la derecha, Fresneda, bala del Sporting portugués, ejerció el cargo con solvencia; en la izquierda, Fran García, mostró el almacén habitual de ímpetu. En la punta, otro novato. No es sencillo hacer de Roberto, el ariete de nuevas que utilizó De la Fuente. Para un delantero de esa especie es como entrar de repente en los Rolling Stones sin desentonar. Lo mismo le sucedió a Serginho en aquel Brasil del 82, una fusta que acompañaba a un centro del campo que parecía haberse caído de una marmita de artistas. Roberto abrió huecos, peleó y cumplió. Los pinceles son de otros. En la puerta checa aparecía Kinsky, célebre en su momento por el concierto que ofreció como portero del Tottenham en el Metropolitano. En esta ocasión, más aseado, aunque exhibió algunos movimientos extraños, nubló algún gol a los rematadores españoles. Lamine Yamal y Baena no comparecieron tras el descanso y dejaron la plaza a Víctor Muñoz y Yeremy Pino. Los checos, con Hlocek como jefe de las travesuras, se acercaron con un gol de Slama. La nube del empate se acercaba. Tras el revuelo por el gol anulado a los checos, España puso el candado al partido. Merino siempre está ahí.

articles.title: Michigan's Kyle Whittingham Says He's Facing 'Biggest Challenge' Of His Career After Minnesota Loss
articles.summary: Not even Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham quite understands the team he has on his hands after the Wolverines suffered a second straight loss on Saturday against Minnesota.
articles.body:
Not even Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham quite understands the team he has on his hands after the Wolverines suffered a second straight loss on Saturday against Minnesota.

"I'm still trying to figure that out," he told reporters when asked if he knew what his team was. "I've been in this profession 40-some years, and this is the biggest challenge I've had. I promise you we're going to figure it out."

The Wolverines have been a roller-coaster ride this season.

There was the controversial 13-12 win over Western Michigan. The team rebounded with wins over then-ranked Oklahoma and UTEP. But consecutive losses to Iowa and Minnesota have restored angst to Ann Arbor.

"Everything's in play," Whittingham told reporters when asked if he would consider making changes with the coaching staff or the starting status of certain players. "We don't want to panic, but everything is being evaluated."

One move that may be coming is a change at quarterback.

Bryce Underwood came to Michigan as a much-hyped 5-star prospect but has yet to live up to the hype. He doubled his interceptions on the season Saturday and has just a 5-to-4 touchdown-to-interception ratio through five games. While he does add value as a runner (212 yards and two scores this season), the issues in the passing game are becoming very hard to ignore.

"We have to go back to square one and figure out what we can fix so we can be the best team we can be," Underwood told reporters after the loss.

Michigan will have a bye before a trip to Happy Valley to face another floundering team in Penn State. After that it's a matchup against Indiana, and the season will close in late November with a brutal stretch—Oregon, UCLA and Ohio State.

In other words, even becoming bowl-eligible is hardly a guarantee for these Wolverines if they don't figure things out, and soon.

articles.title: Yale's Dante Reno Dedicates Comeback Win to Late Father Tony Reno 1 Day After His Death
articles.summary: Yale quarterback Dante Reno dedicated the team's 41-24 comeback victory over Merrimack to his late father, Tony, in a social media post on Saturday.
articles.body:
Yale quarterback Dante Reno dedicated the team's 41-24 comeback victory over Merrimack to his late father, Tony, in a social media post on Saturday.

Yale announced that Tony had died at the age of 52 on Friday.

Tony Reno previously served as the school's football head coach before stepping down due to an illness in February.

On Saturday, Dante helped the Bulldogs erase a 21-7 deficit in the second half to emerge victorious.

The 22-year-old finished 22-of-39 for 298 yards and four touchdowns compared to one interception. He spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different receivers.

Reno also made plays with his legs, rushing for 39 yards on five attempts.

He's in the midst of his second season at Yale after throwing for 2,498 yards and 21 touchdowns while getting picked off 10 times during his 2025 campaign. The Bulldogs finished with a 9-3 record, winning the Ivy League championship.

This year, Reno was making his second appearance of the season after missing a loss vs. Cornell due to an elbow injury.

He's completed 63.4 percent of his passes for 752 yards and nine touchdowns to go along with one interception to open his 2026 campaign.

Tony previously coached the Bulldogs from 2012-25, compiling an 83-49 record while he patrolled the sidelines. Yale won five Ivy League titles during his tenure at the school, as he captured Ivy League Coach of the Year honors in 2022.

With Saturday's win, the Bulldogs improved to 2-1.

articles.title: Beñat San José: "La situación es un poco insostenible"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Rayo Vallecano fue protagonista del evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab desde donde analizó todo lo sucedido en el Trofeo de Vallecas
articles.summary: El entrenador del Rayo Vallecano fue protagonista del evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab desde donde analizó todo lo sucedido en el Trofeo de Vallecas
articles.body: Beñat San José fue uno de los protagonistas del evento de fútbol formativo Skechers Football Lab organizado en Los Ángeles de San Rafael desde donde contó en primera persona como está la situación en la plantilla y en el club tras los acontecimientos sucedidos en el partido correspondiente al Trofeo de Vallecas. PREGUNTA: ¿Cómo valora la situación extradeportiva que está viviendo el Rayo en este inicio de temporada? RESPUESTA: Bueno, a ver, lo primero de todo sí es verdad que el volver al estadio es una ilusión increíble para todos nosotros. El campo lo hemos visto que está muy bien también, que era un debate bastante general. Y la verdad que está muy bien, hemos jugado bien y con comodidad en el campo, adecuadamente. es verdad que el volver a tener contacto con la afición ha sido maravilloso. Y también es verdad, como usted dice, que ha habido tensión, la verdad que es una situación un poco insostenible en ese sentido. Y bueno, nada que decir, al final yo soy entrenador, tampoco puedo expresarme como un directivo, sino como un entrenador. Como entrenador sí puedo decir que nuestra afición, cuando nos apoya, sentimos muchísimo ese apoyo, que es todo el rato. Y que sé perfectamente que a los jugadores les aprecian, les tienen ese cariño, les empujan. Y bueno, cuando hay esos momentos de tensión, pues hay que respetar, siempre y cuando sea pacífico, pues hay que respetar la libertad de expresión que tiene cualquier persona y el aficionado también. Y bueno, a partir de ahí intentar que cuanto antes se normalice, que haya buena armonía entre todos, porque es lo que nos va a ayudar entre todos. Pero bueno, la verdad que es muy incómodo para todos nosotros y obviamente para la propia afición, ¿no? La afición entiendo que no querrá tampoco estar gritando cosas que no sean de ánimo al equipo, ¿no? Entonces, bueno, hemos tenido un poquito ese yin y yang de sensaciones respecto a tensión, pero también de ánimo. Y bueno, siempre lo hemos entendido, lo podemos seguir entendiendo. Y también agradecer a la afición todo el cariño que nos ha transmitido cuando, no solo en el partido, sino que llegando al estadio, después del partido de fuera al estadio también nos ha expresado mucho cariño y yo lo agradezco mucho porque ha acabado de empezar. P: ¿Tiene miedo que los momentos de tensión afecten a la plantilla a nivel deportivo? R: Miedo no es la palabra, pero sí precaución, ¿no? O sea, precaución en qué sentido, en el hecho de que no nos falle la concentración en el partido. Como digo, para nosotros la afición es una parte fundamental y cuando no estén animando porque hay un momento de tensión lo podemos entender y nosotros lo que sí yo como entrenador quiero es que la concentración siga. O sea, con los jugadores, porque notamos esa tensión, pero lo entendemos y punto. Y nosotros a la afición no le pedimos absolutamente nada, sino que nosotros tenemos que dar en el campo y en cuanto de no nos animan, pues es una maravilla porque la verdad que van todos a una y Vallecas es algo muy especial, muy especial. Y bueno, poco más que decir, la verdad. No, yo no he sentido eso en ningún momento, ni nadie me ha dicho absolutamente nada. Todo para nosotros desde en la interna ha ido todo con relativa normalidad y como digo, el campo también estaba bien y el calentamiento también todo ha transcurrido perfectamente y bueno, ha habido momentos que ha podido ser más de tensión. P: ¿Hubo algún riesgo de que no se llegase a jugar el partido del Trofeo de Vallecas? R: Yo no he sentido eso en ningún momento, ni nadie me ha dicho absolutamente nada. Todo para nosotros desde en la interna ha ido todo con relativa normalidad y como digo, el campo también estaba bien y el calentamiento también todo ha transcurrido perfectamente y bueno, ha habido momentos que ha podido ser más de tensión. Yo estaba en el campo, tampoco me he dado cuenta exactamente, pero bueno, es algo que quiero que todos deseamos, incluida la afición, todos, que se vaya solucionando y que sea bueno para todos. P: ¿Ha hablado con Martín Presa? R: No, no, no. No me acuerdo la última vez que hablé con él, pero bueno, algunas veces suele venir a los entrenamientos y alguna vez que nos hemos cruzado y tal, pero poco más. P: ¿Teme que en algún momento tengan que dejar de jugar de nuevo en Vallecas? R: Ni lo pienso ni lo deseo, o sea, no lo deseo pero tampoco lo pienso. Creo que hoy el estadio estaba bien, mientras tenga todas las bases de seguridad y de salubridad, que eso es lo primero, porque la gente lo primero tiene que estar bien. Después el campo, os puedo asegurar que está muy bien, entonces mientras se cumpla eso, la verdad que no tengo ningún temor a que sigamos ahí y ojalá sea así, por supuesto.

articles.title: Yamal on target as Spain hold off Czech Republic
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal continued his superb goalscoring form as Spain secured a 3-1 win over the Czech Republic on Saturday in the Nations League.However Mikel Merino...
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal continued his superb goalscoring form as Spain secured a 3-1 win over the Czech Republic on Saturday in the Nations League.

The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3, after Thomas Tuchel's side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier on in Rijeka.

Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and captain Rodri Hernandez on target but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go.

However Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain's win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July.

"They are well drilled, I thought it would be one of the hardest games and that's how it was," Rodri told Spanish broadcaster TVE after Spain claimed a third win from three group games.

"It was tricky but we got some chances. There are some matches in which you can't generate that much, but the team was able to manage the match."

The former Manchester City midfielder scored for the first time for Spain in over two years.

"It's always special to score for the national team, I'd not been scoring many goals, let's see if I've found that dynamic -- it's important, we all have to chip in with the goals," he added.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday's win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez.

It was one of Spain's star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of.

Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain's first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth before breaking the deadlock.

The 19-year-old winger, a major candidate for the Ballon d'Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curled into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot.

Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal's superb strike. It was the youngster's 11th goal in his last eight games for club and country.

The winger's Barcelona team-mate Rodri doubled Spain's lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him.

De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday's visit to face Croatia.

With the teenager no longer gracing the Carlos Tartiere pitch the pace of the game slowed in the second half.

The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in.

Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise.

Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand.

Czech Republic's determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci's red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez.

Liverpool winger Victor Munoz prodded wide before Merino rounded off the win in the final stages with a finish from close range.

articles.title: UEFA Nations League: Kobel and Aebischer help Switzerland maintain perfect record
articles.summary: Gregor Kobel and Michel Aebischer started for Switzerland as Murat Yakin’s side extended their winning streak with a 2-1 victory over Slovenia. The World Cup...
articles.body:
Gregor Kobel and Michel Aebischer started for Switzerland as Murat Yakin's side extended their winning streak with a 2-1 victory over Slovenia. The World Cup quarter-finalists sit top of Group B1 with a perfect record after three rounds.

Borussia Dortmund's goalkeeper conceded for the first time in Switzerland colours since his World Cup heroics, but Dan Ndoye's strike before half-time secured a 2-1 victory for Nati. Meanwhile, Union Berlin's new midfielder maintained his place after playing the entire game in the 3-0 win against ten-man Scotland in Glasgow.

Fabian Rieder replaced the matchwinner Ndoye for the final few minutes. The Augsburg midfielder has lost his starting berth after the North Macedonia game despite his excellent start to the campaign at club level.

In the other game from Group B1, Scotland once again finished their game with ten players, but they held on to return home with three points after a 2-0 victory over bottom-placed North Macedonia.

Switzerland will host North Macedonia, who are still looking for their first goal of the competition, on Tuesday as they hope to end the international break with four wins out of four.

From League A, Spain also kept their perfect record with a 3-1 win over Czechia in Oviedo. Lamine Yamal scored inside the first six minutes for the third game running before his Barcelona teammate Rodri doubled their advantage.

Czechia showed signs of a comeback with Hoffenheim attacker Adam Hložek providing the assist for Jiri Salama's strike, but the visitors had to finish the game with ten after the second booking for their captain Ladislav Krejčí.

Supersub Mikel Merino sealed the three points before the final whistle as the World Cup champions will now face Croatia in Split. England, who scored seven past Luka Modrić's Croatia, are at home against Czechia as Harry Kane will look forward to more international goals before his return to Säbener Strasse.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham shows potential to be "one of the greatest" as he unlocks new level
articles.summary: It's hard to imagine that just a year ago Jude Bellingham's place in the England squad was up in the air when he is now being talked about as having the potential to be one of England's "greatest of all time".
articles.body:
It's hard to imagine that just a year ago Jude Bellingham's place in the England squad was up in the air. Twelve months on, he is being talked about as having the potential to be one of football's "greatest of all time".

The Real Madrid man was left out of Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions squad in October 2025 and his place at the World Cup was called into question, with the German head coach saying Bellingham wouldn't get star treatment.

But Bellingham did of course make the squad for the World Cup and was arguably his team's standout performer, finishing as their top scorer with seven goals as they reached the semi-finals and finished third.

He has already shown that he is world class with his starring performances for club and country, but the way he helped England to dismantle Croatia 7-0 in the Nations League on Saturday looked like someone potentially reaching a new level.

The 23-year-old was instrumental in Rijeka, scoring as well as registered a hat-trick of assists and ending the match wearing the captain's armband as England inflicted the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history.

"Jude Bellingham can go on to be one of the greatest players of all time," former Manchester United and Republic of Ireland midfielder Roy Keane said on ITV after the game.

"At this moment in time, he is an amazing footballer. The package – his running power, his delivery, his goal threat. The way he is progressing as a player, I still think there is a lot more to come from him."

Bellingham, recently voted England's player of the year for the second year in a row, is now "nailed on as the 10" for the future, former England defender Matt Upson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

And Keane added: "He has been fantastic in possession but what he does out of possession lifts all these other players.

"If you have a player that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and plays for Real Madrid and does brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball will just inspire other players.

'Like on the escalator, you can't stand still'

England's front four will share praise for the way in which they demolished the Croatian backline.

Record goalscorer Harry Kane scored twice, as did Bukayo Saka, with Anthony Gordon scoring and assisting too.

And Kane will gain more headlines on Tuesday when he can equal Peter Shilton's all-time England appearance record against the Czech Republic at Wembley.

In moving to 89 goals for his country, the 33-year-old again showed how irreplaceable he is for England, but, when he was rested with 20 minutes to go, it was Bellingham who took the captain's armband highlighting his importance as a leader with the squad.

He was also directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time in his international career and became the first player to record three assists in a game for the Three Lions since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.

And it was Bellingham's performance in front of goal that impressed former England striker Ian Wright.

"When Bellingham is on the pitch, he is always driving forward and going again and again," he said.

"He was involved in everything. His athleticism, his technical ability, his intensity. He never lets up, the way he gets in the box he is always in there unmarked. He is always in there."

Bellingham showed every aspect of his game against Croatia and Tuchel was asked by BBC Sport if he had gone to another level.

"Yes, at the moment it seems like it, and you always need to," he said.

"It's like you can never stand still. It's like on these electric escalators, if you stand still, you walk against the escalator. You have to walk to even maintain your level.

"You have to develop and you have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up."

Tuchel, who said the performance was a way to "move on" after the disappointment of their World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, said that he "adjusted some things" after the tournament, giving players, including Bellingham, "a lot of responsibility".

Bukayo Saka was part of the front four and Bellingham assisted his first goal with a quality cross.

"He was amazing tonight," Saka said of Bellingham.

"He deserved player of the year and he deserved man of the match tonight too. He was special.

"[I'm] happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."

articles.title: Modric no se muerde la lengua: "Llevo aquí 20 años y es la primera vez que siento vergüenza"
articles.standfirst: Luka alzó la voz tras la contundente derrota que Inglaterra le endosó a Croacia
articles.summary: Luka alzó la voz tras la contundente derrota que Inglaterra le endosó a Croacia
articles.body: Rijeka fue testigo de la goleada endosada a Croacia por parte de Inglaterra. La más abultada de su historia. Luka Modric, que volvía a la titularidad tras descansar ante España, lo vivió en primera persona... y no se mordió la lengua. "Es difícil encontrar una explicación para una actuación como esta sin duelos, faltas, agresividad, falta de unidad... Llevo aquí 20 años, ¡pero por primera vez siento vergüenza después de un partido!", comenzó diciendo el capitán de la selección 'ajedrezada'. "Se puede perder porque, ahora mismo, son mejores. Pero perder así y arruinar la reputación que hemos ganado con los años es inaceptable. Me siento muy avergonzado". Ya en un tono más reflexivo, trató de explicar lo sucedido. "No se puede jugar al fútbol de esta manera. La sensación era que teníamos cuatro o cinco jugadores menos. Fue una noche catastrófica", remarcó. "No debemos culparnos unos a los otros ni buscar culpables, sino estar unidos. Nunca había tenido esta sensación después de un partido". El futuro más próximo no es el más alentador: toca recibir a España tras la goleada recibida en el Pizjuán. "Necesitamos unidos porque nos espera otro partido difícil. Y necesitamos mostrar nuestra verdadera naturaleza, que hay rencor y orgullo en nosotros, deseo, voluntad, unidad, que no se puede perder de la noche a la mañana. Jugar así es inaceptable. Hoy hubiésemos perdido hasta con un equipo de Tercera división". El clima en Rijeka, repleto de niños, fue amigable. Pero, aun así, Modric quiso pedir perdón. "Esperamos que los aficionados de Split estén con nosotros, nos apoyen y que les devolvamos eso de la mejor manera posible. En primer lugar, con espíritu de lucha, siendo luchadores en el campo, que siempre hemos sido, podemos devolver eso. Hoy fue preocupante". Slaven Bilic, seleccionador croata, también salió a dar la cara. "Dios no quiera que vuelva a suceder, Croacia no se merece esto. La responsabilidad recae sobre mí, soy el entrenador, esta es mi selección nacional. Analizaremos todo, pero hay cosas inaceptables". Eso sí, sabe que no puede prometer milagros. "Solo podemos salir adelante con una buena actuación contra España. Es fácil ser bueno y positivo cuando las cosas van bien, es fácil ser amigo cuando las cosas van bien. No puede haber nada más difícil que esto en el fútbol, ahora es el momento: demostremos unidad y carácter. Es absurdo decir que vamos a vencer a España sí o sí, pero tenemos que mostrar una Croacia fuerte y valiente".

articles.title: Xabi Alonso plot to lure Liverpool midfielder to Chelsea in January deal
articles.summary: Chelsea SOLD Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in the closing stages of the summer transfer window. That deal has left a sizeable gap in Xabi Alonso’s midfie...
articles.body:
Chelsea SOLD Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in the closing stages of the summer transfer window.

That deal has left a sizeable gap in Xabi Alonso's midfield with one Liverpool star high up on the Blues boss's wishlist.

Alexis Mac Allister , 27, has made clear his frustrations at not being offered a new contract at Anfield.

With Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai earning bumper new contracts instead the Argentina international has been offered nothing.

Liverpool must weigh up Alexis Mac Allister deal

The FIFA World Cup winner's current deal expires in 2028 - meaning sporting director Julian Ward is in a tough position over the South American.

Either Liverpool earn some money on the No10 in the upcoming windows or else risk losing him for nothing in just under two years' time.

That has put Chelsea on alert according to a report in Football Insider - which claims that a deal for Mac Allister could be wrapped up as soon as January.

Chelsea plot January move for Mac Allister

"Chelsea have set their sights on a move to sign Liverpool star Alexis Mac Allister amid doubts about his long-term future," the report reads.

"Xabi Alonso is determined to strengthen his midfield in January after failing to replace Enzo Fernandez when he made the big-money move to Man City on deadline day.

"Mac Allister is likely to be high on Chelsea's radar as a result, with his potential availability and frustration at Anfield likely placing them on high alert.

"A January move cannot be ruled out, with the Blues stepping up their efforts to strengthen in midfield and Mac Allister held in high regard by the club's hierarchy."

Mac Allister Liverpool future plunged into doubt

Mac Allister moved to Liverpool from Brighton in summer 2023 - for a bargain fee of £35m.

Since then he has become a Premier League champion although his form began to tail off during the 2025/26 season.

The playmaker has recovered some of his form since that contract outburst but we must now wait to see whether any new offer is forthcoming before January.

articles.title: Sin Lamine no fue lo mismo
articles.standfirst: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Tres partidos, 9 puntos y 10 goles marcados. Parece que se puede pedir poco más, pero la segunda parte nos enfrió un poco. No es que haya que achacarlo directamente a ello, pero el bajón se produjo al marcharse Lamine, que sigue de dulce. De la Fuente le pegó una buena sacudida al equipo de salida con eso de la ‘gestión de cargas’ sobre todo en la defensa, pero mantuvo el triángulo de mando del Barça, Rodri-Pedri-Olmo y, sobre todo a Lamine, una atención al buen público ovetense, que agotó las entradas con mucho tiempo de antelación. Decimos constantemente que este equipo funciona igual le cambies las piezas que le cambies, y eso es una verdad casi plena, pero a Lamine hay que dejarle aparte. Es el mejor futbolista del momento. Esta vez le tomó cinco minutos abrir el marcador. Su gol tempranero (ante Inglaterra y Croacia madrugó más) le confirma como el hombre esencial del equipo. El primer gol vale por tres, solía decir Di Stéfano, porque es más difícil de marcar y tiene la utilidad de obligar al rival a remar río arriba. Lamine se ha especializado en ello. La primera parte fue muy buena, en la línea de lo que venimos viendo desde tantos meses acá. Funcionamiento, presión, control, llegada. El partido quedó prácticamente resuelto al descanso y, pena, la segunda mitad no fue lo mismo. Se puede entender, es difícil seguir peleando un partido cuando ya lo consideras ganado, y España permitió que Chequia apareciera y hasta marcó el 2-1 y diríamos que el 2-2, aunque el árbitro dijo que no. En la jugada hay un agarrón a Le Normand, lo que autoriza la anulación, pero para la práctica de estos tiempos pareció una decisión demasiado severa. Pensé que las dos estrellas sobre el escudo ya hacen que los árbitros nos miren con más respeto, así que gracias. Ese gol-no-gol nos dejó ver a un Raya fallón. Ya había hecho un pequeño desastre antes. Su aparición de este sábado consolida a Unai como el primero. Por suerte, el 3-1 final nos permite olvidar ese tanto que se fue al limbo, pero sirva esto para evitar sesteos.

articles.title: Ceballos: "Cambiaría muchos de mis títulos por ganar uno con el Betis"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista confía en que el equipo pueda llegar a los últimos meses del curso peleando por objetivos importantes
articles.summary: El centrocampista confía en que el equipo pueda llegar a los últimos meses del curso peleando por objetivos importantes
articles.body: Dani Ceballos se incorporó al equipo de Manuel Pellegrini en el tramo final del mercado de fichajes de este pasado verano. El utrerano regresó a la que fue su casa nueve años después de su marcha, poniendo así el punto final a una historia alimentada durante años por rumores, guiños y constantes informaciones que apuntaban a un posible regreso al Betis. Ahora, su gran objetivo es cumplir otro sueño: levantar un título con el conjunto verdiblanco. "Obviamente que cambiaría muchos de mis títulos por ganar uno con el Betis", asegura el jugador en el avance de una entrevista con PTV Sevilla publicado en redes. "Pero creo que tenemos que ir paso a paso, plantando bien la dirección a la que queremos ir y a partir de ahí, cuando lleguemos a febrero, marzo o abril veremos en la situación en la que estamos y a ver si podemos hacer grandes cosas", apuntaba. "Hablándolo con compañeros, la Copa del Rey que vivieron hace varios años atrás muchos dicen que nunca habían vivido algo igual. Yo no he tenido la suerte de poderlo vivir, pero ojalá que en estos tres años podamos conseguir algún título", insistió Ceballos. El verdiblanco ha disputado por ahora 73 minutos repartidos en las tres últimas jornadas de LaLiga EA Sports. Se estrenó en la victoria frente al Villarreal, tuvo media hora también en el triunfo por la mínima ante al Getafe y disputó once minutos en el empate contra el Dépor justo antes del presente parón de selecciones.

articles.title: North Macedonia 0-2 Scotland: Sebastien Pocognoli earns first win as captain Andy Robertson hits 100 caps
articles.summary: Match report as Scotland beat North Macedonia; Kieron Bowie opened the scoring with his first international goal; John McGinn doubled the lead from the spot after an earlier penalty decision was overturned; Scotland ended the match 10 men after Scott McKenna's straight red card
articles.body:
The head coach insisted there was no extra pressure after drawing a blank in their opening two Nations League games, but he and the players silenced some critics with a strong performance in Skopje despite a second red card inside a week as they beat North Macedonia 2-0.

Robertson missed two brilliant chances before Kieron Bowie - hooked after Jack Hendry's early sending off against Switzerland in midweek - smashed the ball into the bottom corner to earn his first international goal and Scotland's first in over 420 minutes.

Play was stopped by a dog running onto the pitch before Scotland continued to dominate with Bowie, Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak going close before the break.

Scotland were awarded a penalty when Gannon-Doak went down in the box after half-time, only for the referee to overturn his decision after being called to the monitor.

VAR did then award the visitors a penalty soon after. Rangers striker Bojan Miovski was judged to have stopped Bowie's rebound with his arm after Scott McKenna hit the post.

Questions had been asked about John McGinn's Scotland future but the Aston Villa skipper sent the 'keeper the wrong way to double their lead. It was his 27th goal for his country.

But with the visitors looking comfortable, it was a repeat of Hendry's red on Tuesday as McKenna was sent packing late on for his last-man challenge on Agon Elezi.

Scotland host Solvenia at Hampden Park on Tuesday night in the final Nations League match of this extended international break.

The key moments from the Philip II Arena

5: SAVE! A clean strike from Andy Robertson, a brilliant save from Stole Dimitrievski.

7: GOAL SCOTLAND! Kieron Bowie hammers the ball into the bottom corner from outside the box.

10: CLOSE! Robertson again. The Scotland captain fires wide of the far post with Oli McBurnie screaming for the pass.

10: PITCH INVASION! Well, there's a dog on the pitch. They catch the pooch quickly and the game gets back underway.

13: OVER! Robertson is a man on a mission, with this effort going just over the bar.

28: OVER! Bowie waits for the opening and cuts the ball back to Ben Gannon-Doak, but he gives it too much and it's over.

30: HUGE CHANCE! Bowie chases down the ball and just has to take it around the 'keeper, but it's eventually blocked.

34: SAVE! Dimitrievski does well to hold onto Gannon-Doak's effort from the edge of the box.

50: CHANCE! McGinn does well to set up Gannon-Doak, but he hits it straight at the 'keeper.

51: PENALTY FOR SCOTLAND! Gannon-Doak is brought down as he bursts into the box, and the referee points to the spot.

54: NO PENALTY! The referee is called to the monitor, and after a review it is overturned.

56: SAVE! Brilliant again from Gannon-Doak as he takes a touch before firing towards goal.

57: CLOSE! John McGinn is so close to Scotland's second, but the Aston Villa captain's effort is just wide.

64: PENALTY FOR SCOTLAND! Scott McKenna hits the post and Bowie's rebound looks to be stopped by Bojan Miovski.

69: GOAL SCOTLAND! John McGinn sends the 'keeper the wrong way and Scotland are two up.

83: RED CARD! It was all going so well, but Scott McKenna is sent packing for a last-man challenge on Agon Elezi.

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Scotland about his 100th cap:

"It means everything to me, it means everything to my family.

"I've been away now 100 times, I've got to feel sorry for my wife! It's been an unbelievable journey, I remember my first game and it's been a process since then.

"It's emotional for me. I love this country, there's only one person before me in the men's game to do that, it's a pretty special achievement.

"I thought Kenny Dalglish was going to be worried about his goalscoring record in the first five minutes! I had about six shots.

"They did a nice presentation for me, I told them I wanted the win. The lads did so well to get the win, it'll be a special one for me and my family."

On Scott McKenna's sending off, which came from a tackle after Robertson's short pass, the captain adds: "I apologise for the pass to Scott McKenna, I'll have to go in and apologise to him for that.

"We played really well on a really difficult pitch. We made it a wee bit interesting with the sending off but we defended so well for the last 10 minutes. All of the lads were magnificent and it was a big win. You want to get it as early as possible for the new manager and thankfully we did that tonight."

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli speaking to BBC Scotland.

"I'm very pleased with this first win. But, we stay stable because we have a game in three days, and we want just to have another good game before the end of the first break.

"We played a very good game, we created a lot of chances, we keep two times a zero in three games, which for me means a lot also.

"We played with the right attitude, and for me it was a nice game, not everything was perfect, because we should have scored more goals, but we are in the continuity of the second half from Slovenia, and I hope we can have another good game at home."

On Kieron Bowie's first Scotland goal, he added: "He scored the most difficult one from the game. I was really pleased for him, because I know that the topic about not scoring will be on the table after 25 minutes.

"I was really pleased with his performance, and from many of the lads."
